verified.note: Publication year is 2022, not 2024 -- draft's record carried no year, but verify anyway. Abstract: 'small but significant effects for couple relationship quality (d=.114), relationship skills (d=.132), mental health (d=.074), and coparenting (d=.033), but non-significant effects for relationship stability, parenting, and child well-being'. overall_note: 15 of 17 records fully verified via NCBI E-utilities with strong support (11 PubMed PMIDs KEEP, 2 DOI-resolved KEEP, 1 PMC-resolved KEEP, 1 Cochrane-resolved KEEP). 1 record (ACF meta-analysis, PMID 35040124) is KEEP-with-FIX: the word 'communication' in the draft's claim should be 'relationship skills' to match the abstract's actual outcome label. 2 WHO records (B09860, 9789240117020) could NOT be independently verified with the tools available in this pass (PubMed E-utilities only, no WebFetch/WebSearch) -- both are institutional WHO reports outside PubMed's index; they are marked in-scope but UNFETCHED/UNVERIFIED and should be confirmed directly against who.int/iris.who.int before being cited as settled. One important citation-hygiene finding: the PMC12445309 identifier is a PMC accession number, and a naive PubMed-id lookup on the same numeric string resolves to a completely unrelated 2002 HLA-typing article -- this is a real trap for anyone re-verifying this reference list carelessly; use db=pmc explicitly. No fabricated citations were found among the 15 PubMed/PMC/Cochrane-resolvable records -- all titles, authors, years, and the specific numbers named in the draft's claims (608 million, 18.5 million DALYs, r=0.32/0.27, 68 studies, 62 studies/18 countries, OR 1.84/2.73, 14 studies/10 countries, 31 studies/>25,000/d=0.11/d=0.05, 209 studies/>107,000) were confirmed verbatim or near-verbatim against the actual PubMed abstracts. Per this repo's readout-not-truth / horizontal-knowledge-validation discipline: this verification is itself a readout of what NCBI E-utilities returned on 2026-09-02, not an independent re-derivation of the underlying studies' findings, and the two WHO items remain open items requiring direct WHO-source confirmation, not vertical authority substitution.
